Bhante, in 'web books meditations13 section0032 html 094bd7' (web books meditations13 section0032 html 094bd7), what is the core doctrinal teaching regarding 'This is part of the Buddha’s'?

In this section from *web books meditations13 section0032 html 094bd7*, the master explains: *"This is part of the Buddha’s general teachings on how to get to know your mind at the same time that you’re developing good qualities in the mind."*. From the perspective of the Four Noble Truths, suffering arises whenever the mind grasps at impermanent phenomena (*anicca*) as a reliable self (*atta*). By establishing clear comprehension (*sampajañña*) and seeing conditioned events as empty of inherent ownership, craving (*taṇhā*) is unhooked. It is like grasping a poisonous cobra by the tail: tempting and sleek from afar, but deadly the moment you grasp it. Release the tail and live in safety. Anchor your understanding in direct seeing rather than speculative theory.
